Instrument.name: MAVEN Accelerometer
Instrument.description: The Accelerometer (ACC) on MAVEN spacecraft used atmospheric drag accelerations sensed by inertial measurement units onboard the spacecraft to recover atmospheric density along the orbiter path. These densities are used to estimate hydrostatic, “vertical” density and temperature profiles, along track and altitudinal density waves, and latitudinal and longitudinal density variations. The accelerometer used on MAVEN is a high precision variety, meaning its ‘proof mass’ is an electronically floating body, which is held relatively stationary by varying an electromagnetic field. The ACC is sensitive to acceleration of the center of mass of the spacecraft, centrifugal accelerations due to rigid spacecraft motion, and differences in gravitational force at the proof mass and the spacecraft’s center of mass.
